key_insight: Mixing nanoscale Laponite with microscale Bentonite reduces drying damage, with most intermediate compositions on glass outperforming a simple average of the pure-clay endpoints.
engineering_relevance: Clay composition offers a practical way to improve drying resistance in coatings, barrier layers and ceramic processing.
method: Compare drying damage across clay compositions on hydrophobic polypropylene and hydrophilic glass.
Measure two-step yielding in gelled suspensions and estimate cohesive energy from each step.
Derive a dimensionless cohesion–adhesion index from an energy balance to interpret peeling versus cracking.
evidence_signal: Replicate experiments found essentially intact Laponite films, extensive fracture in Bentonite films and two-step yielding in every composition tested.
watch_item: Yield-step selection changes estimated cohesive energy by orders of magnitude, and critical crack-free thickness versus composition remains unresolved.
paper_title: Resisting Drying Stress in Laponite Bentonite Clay Composites, Two Step Yielding and Crack Peel Selection
